text:
**Short answer:** for most campers, a small 250-300Wh unit like the Jackery Explorer 300 Plus is the best pick. If you need more power for a fridge or a multi-day trip, step up to the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 or Jackery Explorer 2000 v2.

## Weekend tent or car camping (phones, lights, camera, CPAP)
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus (~$249):** PowerStationGearLab's top camping pick. It has 288Wh of LiFePO4 and weighs 8.3 lb. Jackery has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2 on its own site, but the Plus is still sold on Amazon. [Check price](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus (~$269-299):** 286Wh with a 600W inverter, double the Jackery's, and it expands to 572Wh. [Details and buy link](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Anker SOLIX C300 (~$199):** 288Wh with a built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you buy the version with AC outlets, not the "DC" model. OutdoorGearLab scored it lower in its lab tests (50/100), so it's a budget pick rather than a top performer. [Details](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Bluetti EB3A (~$179):** the budget option, with 268Wh and a 600W inverter. [Details](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)

## Mid-size (small fridge, power tools, longer stays)
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2:** OutdoorGearLab's best value for most people. It's under $530 on sale, weighs 25 lb, and has plenty of AC ports. Its fan is noisy and capacity is limited. [Review](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Bluetti AC180 ($499):** 1,152Wh, an 1,800W inverter, about 16 kg (~35 lb) and a 5-year warranty. It has no expansion port. The Dealectric page says code AFF5OFF took $24.95 off in a cart test on 2026-10-21, but checkout has the final word. That page is an affiliate link. [Buy at BLUETTI](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180)

## Multi-day off-grid camping
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2:** OutdoorGearLab's top camping pick (81/100). It has 2,042Wh, weighs 39 lb, and was recently under $900 on Amazon. It can't run a space heater or electric burner for long. [Review](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra (~$1,079):** WIRED's camping pick. It's IP65-rated, has 1,536Wh, and weighs just under 40 lb. [Review](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)

## How to choose
- For phones, lights and a CPAP, 250-500Wh is plenty. Turn off the CPAP humidifier to stretch the battery.
- For a fridge or an electric cooler, aim for 1,000Wh or more.
- A folding solar panel lets you recharge at camp.
- Black Friday is coming, and TechRadar notes prices should drop in November. If your trip isn't soon, it may be worth waiting. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)

Prices come from the review sites and change often. I couldn't verify direct retailer pages for most of these, so confirm the price before buying. Tell me your budget and what you'll run, and I can narrow it to one pick.
